memory_update.text: PLPC should remain the lead underfollowed candidate for the AI/data-center power transmission-hardware chunk because its product layer is closer to a potential grid component chokepoint than downstream EPC names, but survival to later layers requires primary backlog and segment evidence.
PWR and MYRG should be used as downstream demand and procurement timing anchors, not as the main hidden-alpha candidates for the supplier chokepoint lane.

HUBB should be retained as a reference component leader for Utility Solutions order growth, book-to-bill, lead times, and pricing, but it should not crowd out smaller suppliers such as PLPC, ACA, VMI, or AZZ.

ACA and VMI are plausible underfollowed adjacent suppliers to the grid buildout, but both require segment-level evidence that utility transmission/substation demand is driving backlog rather than diversified infrastructure categories.
AZZ remains a speculative shadow relationship because galvanizing and coatings are a logical second-order node, but the company-level link to T&D projects is not yet proven.
LEU belongs in a separate AI-power nuclear-fuel bottleneck lane and should not be scored against grid hardware suppliers without a distinct power-generation/fuel framework.

Need primary filings and earnings-call validation for PLPC, ACA, MYRG, VMI, HUBB, PWR, AZZ, and LEU before Layer 2C scoring; current company-level mappings are mostly inferences from cached Layer 1 context.

For the sulphuric-acid lane, Kpler provides strong commodity-chain evidence, but company-level mapping for SCCO and other copper, nickel, acid, smelter, or logistics names still needs mine-level acid-consumption and procurement evidence.
RHIM.NS remains outside the AI-grid chunk and needs India exchange filings, annual reports, and segment/customer validation before being compared with other New Hotspots candidates.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk around the AI/data-center power grid-upgrade subtheme. The relationship stack separates downstream demand anchors, midstream transmission EPC, direct grid hardware, engineered utility structures, coatings/galvanizing, and adjacent nuclear-fuel power-supply bottlenecks. The cleanest underfollowed relationship remains PLPC as a niche line-hardware supplier whose backlog may provide an early pull-through signal from utility transmission, reconductoring, grid hardening, and data-center interconnection work. ACA, VMI, and AZZ are second-order infrastructure or coatings links that need sharper segment-level evidence. MYRG and PWR are retained as downstream demand/procurement anchors, while HUBB is a reference component leader. LEU is adjacent rather than part of the transmission hardware chain and should be tracked separately as an AI-power reliability/nuclear-fuel bottleneck.

ticker_relationships.node: transmission line hardware and conductor accessories
ticker_relationships.relationship: Most direct underfollowed public-market mapping in this chunk. PLPC sits upstream of utility construction contractors and sells line hardware, formed-wire products, clamps, conductor accessories, and protection hardware that could be pulled forward if AI/data-center load accelerates transmission upgrades, reconductoring, grid hardening, and interconnection work.

ticker_relationships.node: engineered utility structures and infrastructure products
ticker_relationships.relationship: Adjacent supplier to the grid buildout chain. Arcosa may benefit if transmission acceleration increases demand for engineered utility structures, poles, traffic/telecom structures, and related infrastructure products. The relationship is less pure than PLPC because the company is diversified across broader infrastructure and construction products.
